events.title: Constantinople falls to the Ottoman Turks
events.description: After a 53-day siege, Mehmed II's army broke through the city walls; Constantine XI died in the fighting. The Byzantine Empire ended, and Constantinople became the Ottoman capital.
events.html: After a 53-day siege, Mehmed II's army broke through the city walls; Constantine XI died in the fighting. The Byzantine Empire ended, and Constantinople became the Ottoman capital.

events.title: Charles II enters London as the monarchy is restored
events.description: On his 30th birthday, Charles II rode into London to cheering crowds after years of exile. The Restoration ended the republican experiment that had followed his father's execution.
events.html: On his 30th birthday, Charles II rode into London to cheering crowds after years of exile. The Restoration ended the republican experiment that had followed his father's execution.

events.title: Patrick Henry is born in Virginia
events.description: Patrick Henry became one of the most powerful orators of the American Revolution. His 1775 speech ending 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' rallied Virginia to arm.
events.html: Patrick Henry became one of the most powerful orators of the American Revolution. His 1775 speech ending 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' rallied Virginia to arm.

events.title: Wisconsin becomes the 30th US state
events.description: Wisconsin joined the Union from the old Northwest Territory. It later became known for dairy farming and as a centre of the Progressive movement.
events.html: Wisconsin joined the Union from the old Northwest Territory. It later became known for dairy farming and as a centre of the Progressive movement.

events.title: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit of Everest
events.description: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa from Nepal, became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of the world's highest mountain.
events.html: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa from Nepal, became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of the world's highest mountain.

events.title: Nigeria returns to civilian rule
events.description: Olusegun Obasanjo was sworn in as president, ending fifteen years of military government. The date was kept as Nigeria's Democracy Day until 2019, when it moved to 12 June.
